CHAPTER 9

Software Architecture
软件架构

Architecture is about the important stuff…whatever that is.
——Ralph Johnson, computer scientist and co-author of Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software

架构关乎那些重要的东西……不管那到底是什么。
——Ralph Johnson，计算机科学家、《设计模式：可复用面向对象软件的基础》合著者

Software architecture is a massive topic. One of your authors teaches a class on the topic at the University of Minnesota and can only scratch the surface in a semester of graduate school. Seemingly everyone has their own definition of the topic, but they all agree it is important to a project’s long-term success. This chapter won’t make you a software architect, but it will ensure you’ll understand the importance of trade-offs, why the answer is almost always “it depends,” and why quality attributes are key to building applications that can evolve.

软件架构是一个宏大的主题。本书一位作者在明尼苏达大学开这门课，一个学期的研究生课程也只能触及皮毛。似乎每个人对这个话题都有自己的定义，但大家都同意它对项目的长期成功至关重要。本章不会把你变成软件架构师，但它会让你理解权衡（trade-off）的重要性，理解为什么答案几乎总是“看情况”，以及为什么质量属性对于构建可持续演进的应用至关重要。

What Is Architecture?

Have you ever put 20 Agile engineers in a room and asked them each to write down their definition of architecture? I did once. I got 20 different answers.
——Matt Parker, author and engineering leader

你有没有把 20 个敏捷工程师关在一个房间里，让每个人写下自己对架构的定义？我干过一次。我得到了 20 个不同的答案。
——Matt Parker，作家、工程负责人

As discussed in Chapter 4, the software industry is very young and, as such, terminology is often borrowed from more mature disciplines. Architecture is a perfect example: the term comes from the building industry. Before digging the foundation of a new home, an architect designs the structure, making sure the resulting house conforms to the local building codes while also meeting the needs of the future occupants. The architect is responsible for the big picture, the structure, the vision of the project—in other words, the things that are hard to change later, such as electrical, plumbing, and ventilation. Once the concrete is poured, it’s really hard to refactor!

如第 4 章所讨论的，软件行业非常年轻，因此术语常常借自更成熟的学科。架构就是一个绝佳的例子：这个词来自建筑业。在为一栋新房挖地基之前，建筑师会先设计结构，确保建成的房子既符合当地建筑规范，又能满足未来住户的需求。建筑师负责大局、结构、项目的愿景——换句话说，就是那些日后难以更改的东西，比如电路、管道和通风。混凝土一旦浇筑完成，再想重构可就难了！

原书第 221 页

In software, architecture is much the same. On a software project, the architect is responsible for the overall design of the system, taking into consideration all of the often unstated requirements related to scale, performance, security, and the other quality attributes often referred to as the “illities.” While past experience will help you navigate those waters, every application is different. When you encounter an error message from your datastore, an internet search will likely find an answer.1 However, no amount of querying will ever give you a satisfying answer to “Which datastore should I use for the Foo App?”

在软件领域，架构大同小异。在软件项目中，架构师负责系统的整体设计，把所有常常未明说的需求都纳入考虑——这些需求关乎规模、性能、安全性，以及其他常被统称为“-ility”（非功能性质量属性）的东西。虽然过往经验能帮你在这些水域中航行，但每个应用都各不相同。当你遇到数据存储返回的一条报错信息时，上网搜一下多半能找到答案。1然而，无论你怎么搜，都不可能对“我该为 Foo 应用选哪个数据存储？”这个问题得到一个令人满意的答案。

1 Sometimes there are too many answers.
有时候，答案实在太多了。
Architecture is the stuff you can’t Google.
——Neal Ford and Mark Richards, authors of Fundamentals of Software Architecture, 2nd Edition

架构就是那些你谷歌不到的东西。
——Neal Ford 与 Mark Richards，《软件架构基础（第 2 版）》作者

Architecture is sometimes defined as the decisions that are hard to change later. Much as a single-family detached home has different requirements than an apartment building, a software architect must understand the overall landscape of the application. While software can be refactored more easily than a house, some architectural decisions can be devilishly hard to rework later.2 For example, imagine you decide to build your application by breaking it into many small, independent pieces (called microservices) written in Java on top of Spring, only to change your mind six months into the project; you have a challenge ahead of you. Architecture requires critical thinking! Architects identify the key quality attributes for a given project and ensure that the design meets those requirements.

架构有时被定义为“那些日后难以更改的决策”。正如独栋住宅与公寓楼有不同的需求，软件架构师也必须理解应用的整体格局。虽然软件比房子更容易重构，但有些架构决策事后再改会难得要命。2例如，想象你决定把应用拆成许多小而独立的片段（称为微服务），用 Java 基于 Spring 编写，结果项目进行到六个月时你改了主意——那你面前可有得忙了。架构需要批判性思考！架构师要为特定项目识别关键质量属性，并确保设计满足这些要求。

2 While you cannot predict the future, good architectural decisions can make it simpler to change things in the future by carefully considering how the application is likely to evolve.
虽然你无法预测未来，但好的架构决策会通过审慎考量应用可能如何演进，让日后的变更变得更容易。

Ultimately, architecture is about making decisions about things that are difficult to change later based on trade-off analysis. As such, architects will take time to explore the problem space in an effort to ensure that the application can meet more than just its functional requirements. An architect will often ask questions like these:

归根结底，架构就是基于权衡分析，对那些日后难以更改的事情做决策。因此，架构师会花时间探索问题空间，以确保应用不仅能满足功能需求。架构师常常会问这样一些问题：

  • How many users does this application have to support? How many of those are concurrent?这个应用需要支持多少用户？其中有多少是并发的？
  • Where are those users located? Are they mostly in the same area, or are they spread out around the world?这些用户分布在哪里？是大多集中在同一地区，还是遍布全球？
  • What is the availability target for this application?这个应用的可用性目标是多少？
  • What can cause a spike in demand or usage of the application?什么会导致应用的需求或使用量骤增？
  • When will this application typically be used? Business hours? Any time of day?这个应用通常在什么时候被使用？工作时间？一天中的任何时候？
  • What constraints exist? What does this application integrate with?存在哪些约束？这个应用要和什么集成？
原书第 222 页
  • Which cloud provider(s) does the organization contract with?公司与哪些云服务商签了约？
  • What is the competitive landscape? What does your competition require you to match or exceed?竞争格局如何？竞争对手要求你对标或超越什么？
  • What is the ideal deployment environment?理想的部署环境是什么样？
  • What is the current deployment environment?当前的部署环境是什么样？
  • What data should the application store? How long should that data be retained?应用应当存储什么数据？这些数据应保留多久？
  • What is the carbon footprint of the application, and how can it be optimized?应用的碳足迹是多少？如何优化？
  • What is the cost of this application, and how can it be optimized?这个应用的成本是多少？如何优化？
  • What laws and regulations must be adhered to?必须遵守哪些法律法规？
  • What are acceptable response times for various aspects of the systems?系统各个部分可接受的响应时间是多少？
  • What security policies must this application meet or exceed?这个应用必须满足或超越哪些安全策略？
  • What privacy concerns does this application have?这个应用涉及哪些隐私问题？

These questions have no generic answers, as your applications are unique! That is why there is no “right answer” when it comes to choosing an architecture. You must weigh the pros and cons of every decision. For example, if you’re building a document management system for 300 people in Brazil, you’d locate your application in data centers in or near Brazil, you’d want to consult your legal department to understand any specific laws or regulations in the Brazilian market, and you’d want to know how many documents the application was expected to process a month as well as how large those documents typically are. It’d also be wise to ask if there were any plans to expand beyond Brazil, if there would be a need for any document translation, and what type of document analysis would need to be supported.

这些问题没有通用答案，因为你的应用是独一无二的！这就是为什么在选择架构时没有“正确答案”。你必须权衡每个决策的利弊。例如，如果你要为巴西的 300 人构建一个文档管理系统，你会把应用部署在巴西境内或附近的数据中心，会咨询法务部门了解巴西市场的特定法律法规，还会想知道应用预计每月处理多少文档、这些文档通常有多大。明智的做法还包括问一问：是否有扩张到巴西以外的计划、是否需要文档翻译、以及需要支持哪种类型的文档分析。

Trade-Offs

Programmers know the benefits of everything and the trade-offs of nothing. Architects need to understand both.
——Rich Hickey, creator of the Clojure programming language

程序员知道一切事物的好处，却不知道任何事物的取舍。架构师则两者都要懂。
——Rich Hickey，Clojure 编程语言之父

Architecture concerns itself with the questions that don’t have a simple answer, which is why architects answer nearly every question with, “It depends.”3 In school you learned there was an answer that got you an A, an answer that got you a B, and an answer that got you a C. However, in software, to quote Neal Ford, “There are no right or wrong answers in architecture—only trade-offs.” And to further complicate matters, in software, there isn’t a “best” answer; in most cases you will have to accept the least worst answer. Every decision you make on a software project involves a trade-off.4

架构关心的是那些没有简单答案的问题，所以架构师几乎对每个问题都回答“看情况”。3在学校里你学到的是：有一个答案能让你得 A，一个答案得 B，一个答案得 C。然而在软件领域，套用 Neal Ford 的话说：“架构里没有对错答案——只有权衡。”更复杂的是，软件里也没有“最好”的答案；在大多数情况下，你只能接受“最不差”的那个答案。你在软件项目中做的每个决策都涉及权衡。4

3 Your authors may even wear “It Depends” T-shirts to save time in meetings.
本书作者甚至会穿印有“It Depends”的 T 恤，以在会议上节省时间。
4 And, for that matter, every decision you make in life.
而且，说起来，你人生中做的每个决策也都如此。
原书第 223 页

An architect’s job is to perform the trade-off analysis on the (many) options you will consider for a given project. Every architectural style can be said to have various “star ratings” across various architectural characteristics, but the analysis isn’t just as simple as picking the one with the most stars. Certain characteristics might matter more for your application than others, thus pushing you toward a style that may appear less than ideal at first glance. Many projects fail in their attempt to create an academically perfect architecture, something that isn’t attainable. Good architects make the best decisions they can while still meeting project deadlines.

架构师的工作，就是针对给定项目所考虑的（众多）选项做权衡分析。每种架构风格都可以说在不同架构特征上有各自的“星级评分”，但分析并不只是挑星级最高的那个那么简单。某些特征对你的应用可能比另一些更重要，从而把你推向一种乍看之下并不那么理想的风格。许多项目在试图构建学术上完美的架构时失败了——而那种架构根本不可能实现。优秀的架构师会在满足项目工期的前提下，做出他们能做的最佳决策。

The Accidental Architect
意外的架构师

Many organizations can be a bit…territorial…with titles, and it is very common for engineers to perform architectural tasks even without holding the title of architect, something your authors can personally attest to. We’ve also never seen an organization that had more architects than they knew what to do with, and most architects are spread thin across many projects. You may find yourself with limited (or no) access to “an architect,” making you the accidental architect. If you find yourself playing the role of architect, make sure you’re taking the time to see the bigger picture and don’t be afraid to get feedback from your team and others in your organization.
许多公司在头衔上可能有点……地盘意识……工程师即便没有架构师头衔，也在干架构师的活，这种情况非常普遍——本书作者可以亲身作证。我们也从没见过哪家公司架构师多到不知道该怎么安排的，大多数架构师都被摊派到许多项目上，分身乏术。你可能会发现自己能接触到的“架构师”很有限（甚至根本没有），于是你成了那个“意外的架构师”。如果你发现自己在扮演架构师的角色，一定要花时间去看大局，别怕向团队和公司里的其他人征求反馈。

You must perform due diligence to weigh the trade-offs. For example, engineers will often pull out common functionality used across modules into a reusable library to facilitate reuse and simplify maintenance. However, should that library be a service that is called at runtime or a library that is built with the caller? In other words, should it be a runtime dependency or a build-time dependency? It depends! But what does it depend on? You can assess a few factors in this situation. You might first ask how volatile the library is, how frequently does it change? Relatedly, how critical is it for callers to have the latest version? If the library is in near constant flux, a runtime dependency would make sense; you can deploy new versions of the library as needed, and you can rest assured every caller will have the latest version at the same time.

你必须做尽职调查来权衡利弊。例如，工程师常常把各模块共用的功能抽出来做成一个可复用库，以便复用并简化维护。但是，这个库应该是一个在运行时调用的服务，还是一个随调用方一起构建的库？换句话说，它应该是运行时依赖还是构建时依赖？看情况！那到底取决于什么？在这种情况下你可以评估几个因素。你可能首先会问这个库变动有多频繁？它多久变一次？与此相关，调用方用上最新版本有多重要？如果这个库几乎一直在变，运行时依赖就说得通；你可以按需部署新版本，而且可以放心，每个调用方会同时用上最新版本。

However, you’ve introduced an out-of-process call into your application, which provides surface area for a new set of errors. What does your application do if it cannot reach the external library service? Does that library need to be geographically distributed? Depending on what the library did, you might have to include an alternative, a cached answer, or a default result. If you choose to make the library a build-time dependency, you remove any network hops, which removes a set of errors and is simpler to test. Upgrades to that library are now more difficult to roll out to an organization, though, and there’s a strong likelihood different users of that library will deploy with different versions.

然而，你给应用引入了一次进程外调用，这就为一整类新错误提供了可乘之机。如果应用连不上那个外部库服务，它该怎么办？那个库需要做地理分布吗？根据这个库的职责不同，你可能得准备一个替代方案、一个缓存的答案或一个默认结果。如果你选择把这个库做成构建时依赖，就消除了所有网络跳转，也就消除了一类错误，测试也更简单。不过，把这个库的升级推广到整个组织会变得更困难，而且这个库的不同使用者极有可能部署着不同的版本。

好东西比坏东西好，除非并非如此。

另外，没有什么是绝对的好或坏。

看情况。
The answer to every question is “it depends,” except for when it doesn’t. It depends.
每个问题的答案都是“看情况”，除非不是。看情况。
Name three things you like. You can’t have them at the same time.
说出三样你喜欢的东西。你不可能同时都拥有。

不行。
There are many definitions of software architecture, but none of them are correct.
软件架构有很多定义，但没有一个是对的。

软件架构这种东西根本不存在。

——Ken Scrambler

Which approach is “correct”? It depends! For example, consider a utility that calculates sales tax based on the shipping destination. Clearly that can change on a regular basis, and it’s important for the system to use the most up-to-date rules, but if a network issue prevents your application from calculating tax, there better be a backup in place, or you should expect an urgent message from people high up in the organizational chart. What would you recommend in this situation?

哪种做法才“正确”？看情况！例如，考虑一个根据收货目的地计算销售税的工具。税率显然会定期变动，系统使用最新规则很重要；但如果网络问题导致你的应用无法计算税款，最好有个备用方案，否则你就等着收到组织架构图高层发来的紧急消息吧。在这种情况下，你会推荐什么？

Architecture Versus Design

The boundaries between architecture and design are fuzzy. On any given project, design decisions will affect the architecture, and vice versa. This is sometimes referred to as the Twin Peaks Model, describing the many chicken-and-egg situations often found on a software project. In this case, the current design may limit your architectural maneuverability, and the current architecture will impact your design space! Some decisions will neatly fit into either the architecture or design bucket, but the vast majority live along a continuum between the two. For example, choosing which architectural style is best for your application is clearly an architectural decision, while choosing a data type in a class is a design decision.

架构与设计之间的界限是模糊的。在任何项目上，设计决策都会影响架构，反之亦然。这有时被称为双峰模型（Twin Peaks Model），描述软件项目中常见的种种“先有鸡还是先有蛋”的局面。在这种局面下，当前的设计可能限制你的架构回旋余地，而当前的架构又会影响你的设计空间！有些决策可以干净利落地归入架构或设计的某一桶，但绝大多数都落在两者之间的连续体上。例如，为应用选择哪种架构风格显然是架构决策，而在一个类里选哪种数据类型则是设计决策。

If the distinction between architecture and design is often a matter of degrees, does the distinction matter? It depends! In many cases, it comes down to who is best positioned to make the ultimate decision. Architects and developers should be prepared (and willing) to work together on those decisions that fall between the two ends of the continuum.

如果架构与设计的区分往往只是程度问题，那这个区分重要吗？看情况！在很多情况下，它归结为谁最有资格做最终决策。对于那些落在连续体两端之间的决策，架构师和开发者都应当准备好（并且愿意）携手合作。

原书第 225 页

Another lens you can apply is to ask yourself: is this decision strategic or tactical? Strategic thinking requires you to think ahead, focusing on long-term goals and the overall direction of the project. In many cases, the strategic thing to do might take a bit longer or even require you to backtrack a bit.5 Tactical decisions are often short-term actions that solve an immediate, acute problem that may require a longer-term solution at a later date.6 Think of it as the equivalent of securing something with duct tape, knowing it isn’t a permanent fix.

你还可以换一个视角，问自己：这个决策是战略性的还是战术性的？战略性思考要求你向前看，聚焦于长期目标和项目的整体方向。在很多情况下，做战略性的事可能要多花一点时间，甚至需要你回退几步。5战术性决策通常是短期行动，用来解决一个眼下紧迫的问题，而这个问题日后可能还需要一个更长期的解决方案。6你可以把它想象成用胶带把东西固定住，心里清楚这不是长久之计。

5 Take the time it takes so it takes less time.
该花的时间花到位，往后才更省时间。
6 Don’t be surprised when that short-term fix is still running years later.
当那个临时解决方案多年后还在跑时，别惊讶。

The more tactical a decision, the closer it is to design. The more strategic a decision, the more it veers into architecture. How many people does it take to make the decision? What are their roles? Anything that can be decided by a developer or two is a prime example of a tactical decision. If a decision requires weeks of meetings up to and including the CTO, it’s strategic.

一个决策越偏战术，就越接近设计；越偏战略，就越滑向架构。做这个决策需要多少人？他们是什么角色？一两个开发者就能拍板的事，是战术决策的典型例子。如果一个决策需要开几周的会、一路上升到 CTO 才能定，那就是战略性的。

Another way of looking at the difference is to ask yourself: what is the cost of change? Refactoring a method is mechanical and can be done by your IDE. Changing the signature on a widely used service is not. Refactoring a method is tactical; refactoring a monolith into microservices is strategic. Naming a method is tactical,7 but naming an external service used by countless customers is strategic. Throughout any project, you will face countless tactical and strategic choices, and you will often have to make decisions with incomplete information and insufficient time.

看待这个区别的另一个角度是问自己：变更的成本是什么？重构一个方法是机械性的，IDE 就能搞定；修改一个被广泛使用的服务的签名则不然。重构方法是战术，把单体重构为微服务是战略。给方法起名是战术，7但给一个被无数客户使用的外部服务起名就是战略。在任何项目中，你都会面对无数战术与战略抉择，而且常常不得不在信息不完整、时间不充裕的情况下做决策。

7 Which isn’t to diminish its importance or its ability to spark a spirited debate.
这并不是要贬低它的重要性，也不是说它引不起激烈的争论。

Quality Attributes

As discussed earlier, an architect’s focus is broader than the feature and functionality of the application; they have to think about the quality attributes necessary to deliver the complete solution. These are sometimes referred to as nonfunctional requirements, the architectural characteristics, quality goals, constraints, quality of service goals, the architecturally significant requirements or, more colloquially, the “illities.”8 One of your most important jobs as an architect is to understand the quality attributes that matter most to your application.

如前所述，架构师的关注点比应用的特性和功能更宽；他们必须思考交付完整方案所需的质量属性。这些有时被称为非功能性需求、架构特征、质量目标、约束、服务质量目标、架构重要需求，或者更口语化地叫“-ility”们。8作为架构师，你最重要的工作之一就是理解对你的应用最重要的那些质量属性。

8 The running joke is that simply adding the suffix -illity to any word results in something an architect cares about.
流传的玩笑是：随便给哪个词加上后缀 -ility，结果就是架构师关心的东西。
原书第 226 页

Nonfunctional Requirements
非功能性需求

Many of you may be familiar with the idea of nonfunctional requirements and may wonder why we don’t use that common term. Our choice boils down to this realization over many years: when you talk to a stakeholder about nonfunctional things, they often stop listening as they (consciously or not) think, “I don’t want any of that nonfunctional stuff, focus on my business requirements.”
你们中很多人可能熟悉非功能性需求这个概念，也许会奇怪我们为什么不用这个常见说法。我们的选择归结为多年来的一个体会：当你和某个干系人谈论非功能性的事情时，他们常常就不听了，因为他们（自觉或不自觉地）在想：“我可不要那些非功能性的玩意儿，聚焦到我的业务需求上。”
Stakeholders are often laser-focused on what they need the application to do, which is important; you need to meet those needs. But you also need to see the bigger picture, the considerations most stakeholders aren’t thinking about. Using the quality attributes changes the tenor of the conversation. Most customers are delighted to discuss quality.
干系人往往高度聚焦于他们需要应用做什么——这很重要，你必须满足这些需求。但你也需要看到大局，看到大多数干系人没在考虑的那些因素。改用质量属性这个说法，会改变谈话的基调。大多数客户都很乐意讨论质量。

You are likely familiar with several quality attributes such as maintainability, scalability, reliability, security, deployability, simplicity, usability, compatibility, fault tolerance—the list is long.9 Which quality attributes matter most to you? It depends!10 The type of applications you build determine which of these are most important. For example, if you are writing a device driver, performance may be far more important than maintainability, while an ecommerce platform will prioritize availability and scalability.

你可能已经熟悉好几个质量属性了，比如可维护性、可扩展性、可靠性、安全性、可部署性、简洁性、可用性、兼容性、容错性——这个清单很长。9哪些质量属性对你最重要？看情况！10你构建的应用类型决定了其中哪些最重要。例如，如果你在写设备驱动，性能可能远比可维护性重要；而电商平台则会优先考虑可用性和可扩展性。

9 More architects should strive for simplicity.
更多架构师应该去追求简洁。
10 We weren’t kidding about “it depends” being the answer to every question in architecture.
“架构里每个问题的答案都是看情况”——我们可不是在开玩笑。

To make matters more complicated, you can’t turn every knob up to 11 either. In fact, some quality attributes have inverse relationships with each other: maximizing one will minimize another. Security and usability can sometimes be at odds with each other. You could design a system that is completely secure, not connect it to the network, run it in a locked room, and better yet, not have a login screen. While secure, it certainly isn’t very usable.

让事情更复杂的是，你也不能把每个旋钮都拧到 11。事实上，有些质量属性之间存在反向关系：把一个拉到最大，另一个就会被压到最小。安全性和可用性有时会相互冲突。你可以设计一个完全安全的系统：不连网络、放在一个锁起来的房间里运行，更妙的是连登录界面都不要。它是安全了，但肯定谈不上好用。

Your challenge is to identify the quality attributes, then orient them in the correct tension with one another. Additionally, you often have to convince your stakeholders of the value of some of the less visible quality attributes.

你的挑战在于识别这些质量属性，然后让它们彼此保持恰当的张力。此外，你常常还得说服干系人，让他们相信那些不那么显眼的质量属性的价值。

Identifying Quality Attributes

How do you know what quality attributes matter on a project? Certain words and phrases should stand out to you that signal quality attributes. For example, consider the following Concert Comparison kata.

你怎么知道一个项目上哪些质量属性重要？有些词语和短语应当引起你的警觉，它们就是质量属性的信号。例如，请看下面这个“演唱会对比”道场题。

原书第 227 页

A concert ticketing site with big acts and high volume needs an elastic solution to sell tickets:

一个大牌云集、流量巨大的演唱会票务网站，需要一个有弹性的解决方案来卖票：

  • Users: Thousands of concurrent users, bursts of up to 10,000/second when tickets go on sale.用户：数千并发用户，开票瞬间峰值可达每秒 10,000 次。
  • Requirements:需求：
    • Allow concurrent ticket buying.允许并发购票。
    • Do not sell a seat more than once!一个座位绝不能卖两次！
    • Shoppers can see an overview of remaining seats.购票者能看到剩余座位的概览。
  • Additional context:额外背景：
    • Consider an implementation in both space-based and microservices architecture style.分别用基于空间（space-based）和微服务两种架构风格实现。
    • Identify the trade-offs for each solution.指出每种方案的权衡。

Reading through these requirements, a few things should catch your eye. Having thousands of concurrent users with huge bursts when tickets go on sale implies a highly scalable solution that is also very resilient.11 And it can likely scale down to near zero after the initial surge of activity.

通读这些需求，有几样东西应当引起你的注意。数千并发用户加上开票瞬间的巨大峰值，意味着需要一个高可扩展、同时又非常有韧性的方案。11而且在最初的活动高峰过后，它很可能需要能缩容到接近于零。

11 Can you say Taylor Swift?
你能说出 Taylor Swift 吗？（指代其演唱会门票秒空的盛况。）

Obviously, you can’t sell the same seat twice, meaning you’ll need to come up with a way of locking a seat but in a manner that doesn’t allow individual users to block out dozens or hundreds of seats. Oh, and unstated here, but what is your solution to weed out bots?

显然，同一个座位不能卖两次，这意味着你得想出一种锁定座位的办法，但又不能让单个用户把几十个甚至上百个座位都占住。哦，还有一点这里没写出来：你用什么方案来甄别机器人（抢票脚本）？

Once you have an idea of which quality attributes matter most for your situation, take time to rank them. Ordering can be done with a mind map, a table, or even just a numbered list. Once you have your list ready, it’s time to get feedback. Share your artifact with interested stakeholders, consider their feedback, and iterate.

一旦你对哪些质量属性在你的情境下最重要有了概念，就花时间给它们排个序。排序可以用思维导图、表格，甚至就是一个编号列表。列表就绪后，就该去征求反馈了。把你的成果分享给相关干系人，考虑他们的反馈，然后迭代。

Gaining Stakeholder Alignment

Speaking of interested stakeholders, how do you get a stakeholder to understand the importance of a quality attribute? This is where your influencing skills can come in handy (see Chapter 13 for more on practicing influence and managing stakeholders). While explaining the importance of security to a decision maker may be straightforward, helping them understand the value in maintainability or simplicity requires you to flex your influence muscles.

说到相关干系人，你怎么让一个干系人理解某个质量属性的重要性？这时候你的影响力就能派上用场了（关于练习影响力和管理干系人，详见第 13 章）。向决策者解释安全性的重要性可能直截了当，但要让他们理解可维护性或简洁性的价值，就需要你活动一下影响力的肌肉了。

You can start by outlining the benefits of quality attributes by using terms and examples that are relevant to them. Be careful you aren’t framing things purely in a technical manner; while important to you, customers, for example, really shouldn’t concern themselves with purely technical choices.12 Find common ground and have a conversation with them about their concerns. While you may not think their concerns are important, hear them out: there is almost always a nugget to mine, and it’s important to consider their concerns. At the end of the day, a conversation needs to take place.

你可以先用与他们相关的术语和例子，把质量属性的好处讲清楚。注意别纯粹用技术口吻来表述；比如，客户虽然对你很重要，但他们实在不该为纯技术选择操心。12找到共同点，和他们聊聊他们关心的事。哪怕你觉得他们的顾虑不重要，也先听完：几乎总能从中淘到金子，而且考虑他们的顾虑很重要。归根结底，对话是必须发生的。

12 And frankly some of the worst customers to work with are those who think they know more about software than you do.
坦白说，最难合作的客户，就是那些自以为比你更懂软件的客户。
原书第 228 页

It is also important for you to find the influential people in your organization, which often has little to do with the organizational chart. As an architect, you won’t always have a direct line of sight to the decision maker. You may have to work through someone else to get what you want accomplished. Approach as an equal, and rely on the strength of your ideas and your reputation. Find common ground and wield the power of reciprocity.

对你来说，找到公司里有影响力的人也很重要——而这往往和组织架构图关系不大。作为架构师，你并不总能直接联系到决策者。你可能得通过别人才能把事情办成。以平等的姿态接触对方，依靠你想法的说服力和你的声誉。找到共同点，运用互惠的力量。

A reform often advances most rapidly by indirection.
——Frances Willard, American temperance activist and suffragist

一项改革往往是通过迂回的方式推进得最快。
——Frances Willard，美国禁酒运动活动家、妇女参政论者

The Power of Indirection
迂回的力量

Nate here. Years ago, I tried to introduce Git into an organization. We put together a very compelling argument (as a gist no less) outlining why we wanted to replace our existing version control tool. Our presentation earned the go-ahead from our architecture group; however, once we tried to convince the team that managed the existing tool, we were shut down. Hard. We were informed that we already had a tool and that they weren’t open to anything new.
我是 Nate。多年前，我试图把 Git 引入一家公司。我们写了一份非常有说服力的论证（还是用 gist 写的），说明了为什么要替换现有的版本控制工具。我们的汇报拿到了架构组的批准；然而，当我们试图说服管理现有工具的那个团队时，我们被回绝了。被坚决回绝。我们被告知已经有一个工具了，他们对任何新东西都不开放。
We took a step back and recruited a more influential ally, the person who acted as the right hand of the CTO.13 After explaining our approach, he had a powerful insight: don’t introduce Git as a replacement but rather as a complement to our existing toolkit. He positioned Git as a solution to our code collaboration problem, a tool that would enable us to more easily share artifacts. This indirect approach was enough to deactivate the negative sentiment from the team that supported the existing tool; after all, it was additive.14 We quickly spun up a pilot, discovered multiple opportunities for reuse, and had an enterprise-wide solution set up within a few months.
我们退了一步，招募了一位更有影响力的盟友——那位充当 CTO 左右手的人。13在我们解释了方案之后，他有了一个强有力的洞见：别把 Git 作为替代品引入，而要作为现有工具包的补充。他把 Git 定位为解决代码协作问题的方案、一个能让我们更轻松地共享产物的工具。这种迂回的做法足以化解支持现有工具那个团队的抵触情绪；毕竟，这是增量式的。14我们很快搞了个试点，发现了多处可复用的机会，几个月内就建起了一套全公司范围的解决方案。
The lesson? The direct path often leads to the most resistance. Consider an alternative approach or framing when introducing new ideas, technologies, and tools.
教训是什么？直接的路径往往遭遇最大的阻力。在引入新想法、新技术和新工具时，不妨考虑换一种方式或换一种表述。
13 No, that isn’t actually a title on the org chart, but it was clear this person was respected by leadership.
不，这其实不是组织架构图上的一个头衔，但很明显这个人受到领导层的尊重。
14 It also helped that the proposal was introduced by someone with more organizational clout.
提案是由一位在组织里更有分量的人提出的，这也帮了忙。
原书第 229 页

Architectural Styles

After identifying the key quality attributes for your application, you can analyze and choose the proper architectural style. An architectural style describes the overall structure of the code as well as how it interacts with the datastore. You can choose from any number of styles for an application, and as you can probably guess, there’s no one-size-fits-all solution.

识别出应用的关键质量属性之后，你就可以分析并选择合适的架构风格了。架构风格描述了代码的整体结构，以及它如何与数据存储交互。一个应用可以从任意多种风格中选择，而正如你可能猜到的，没有放之四海而皆准的方案。

Broadly speaking, architectural styles can be categorized into two main types: monolithic (a single deployable unit) or distributed (multiple deployable units). While monoliths are often derided as being unmaintainable, the fault lies with a poorly structured system, not the deployment topology. Maintainable modular monoliths are possible, and without the proper discipline and attention to technical debt, heavily distributed systems can be extremely challenging to evolve.

广义上讲，架构风格可分为两大类：单体式（单个可部署单元）或分布式（多个可部署单元）。虽然单体常被嘲讽为不可维护，但问题出在结构糟糕的系统，而不是部署拓扑。可维护的模块化单体是可能的；而如果没有恰当的纪律和对技术债的关注，高度分布式的系统演进起来可能极具挑战。

Monolithic styles include the big ball of mud, layered, microkernel, and pipeline. Distributed styles include space based, service oriented, microservices, and event driven. A full accounting of the various architectural styles is beyond the scope of this book.15 However, it is important to understand that each architectural style has different strengths and weaknesses across the various architectural characteristics.

单体风格包括大泥球、分层、微内核和管道。分布式风格包括基于空间、面向服务、微服务和事件驱动。对各种架构风格的完整论述超出了本书范围。15然而，重要的是要理解：每种架构风格在不同架构特征上都有不同的优缺点。

15 For a complete discussion, see Fundamentals of Software Architecture by Mark Richards and Neal Ford (O’Reilly, 2022).
完整讨论见 Mark Richards 与 Neal Ford 所著《Fundamentals of Software Architecture》（O’Reilly，2022）。

For example, a microservices architecture gives you excellent elasticity and scalability but comes with additional network hops, which can hurt performance, and increased complexity and cost compared to other options. Microservices also require monitoring and observability, and it can be challenging to debug and trace errors.

例如，微服务架构给你出色的弹性和可扩展性，但代价是额外的网络跳转——这可能损害性能——以及与其他方案相比更高的复杂性和成本。微服务还需要监控和可观测性，调试和追踪错误也可能很有挑战。

Choosing the correct style is all about trade-offs. If your application needs scalability and elasticity, microservices can be an excellent choice. But if those aren’t key characteristics, another style is probably a better option. The right approach for one application could be wrong for another. Again, there’s no way to search the internet for “What architectural style should I use?”16 You have to look at the trade-offs. Identifying the proper architectural style for a given situation is one of the most important things an architect does.

选择正确的风格，关键全在权衡。如果你的应用需要可扩展性和弹性，微服务可能是绝佳选择。但如果这些不是关键特征，另一种风格或许更合适。对一个应用正确的做法，对另一个应用可能就是错的。再说一遍，你没法在网上搜“我该用哪种架构风格？”16你必须去看权衡。为特定情境识别合适的架构风格，是架构师最重要的工作之一。

16 It depends.
看情况。

The Agile Architect

Architecture is often defined as the decisions that are hard to change later, but change is the one constant in technology. Does that mean architecture is inherently antithetical to Agile projects? Some organizations (proudly) proclaim that they are Agile and as such don’t have architects. Regardless of titles, you have people making architectural decisions on your projects. Hopefully, they’re making good ones: you’ll know in a year or two if they did.

架构常被定义为“日后难以更改的决策”，但变化是技术领域唯一不变的东西。这是否意味着架构天生就与敏捷项目对立？有些组织（自豪地）宣称自己是敏捷的，因此不需要架构师。无论头衔如何，你的项目上总有人在做架构决策。希望他们做的是好决策：一两年后你就会知道他们做得好不好。

原书第 230 页

Architecture and agility can absolutely coexist, though some, perhaps most, architectural activities won’t complete within an iteration boundary.17 Creating an agile architecture may require you to change your assumptions a bit, though. Instead of trying to create an architecture that can effortlessly handle future requirements, what if you designed your architecture expecting things to change? That idea is one of the core tenets of evolutionary architecture.

架构与敏捷完全可以共存，尽管有些（也许是大多数）架构活动不会在一个迭代边界内完成。17不过，构建敏捷架构可能需要你稍微改变一下自己的假设。与其试图创造一种能不费吹灰之力应对未来需求的架构，不如把架构设计成“预期事物会变化”的样子？这个想法正是演进式架构的核心原则之一。

17 If you’ve ever worked with procurement or legal, you quickly realize you are not in control of the schedule.
如果你和采购或法务部门打过交道，很快就会意识到进度并不掌握在你手里。
An evolutionary architecture supports guided, incremental change across multiple dimensions.
——Building Evolutionary Architectures, 2nd ed., by Neal Ford et al.

演进式架构支持跨多个维度的、有指导的、增量式的变更。
——Neal Ford 等著《演进式架构（第 2 版）》

Evolutionary architectures allow you to change incrementally as required by shifting business needs, priorities, and technological change. The key word here is incremental. Agile software development is ultimately about nested feedback loops. Rather than spend months working on a bunch of features only to discover you’ve missed the mark, regular demonstrations provide opportunities for key stakeholders to react and adjust to actual working software. Hypothesis-driven development is one method that can help you gather data and proceed accordingly.

演进式架构允许你根据业务需求、优先级和技术变化的转移，增量式地做出改变。这里的关键词是“增量”。敏捷软件开发归根结底是关于嵌套的反馈回路。与其花几个月做一堆功能、结果却发现没打中靶心，不如通过定期演示让关键干系人有机会对真正可运行的软件做出反应和调整。假设驱动开发是一种方法，能帮你收集数据并据此前进。

Hypothesis-driven development utilizes a structure like this:

假设驱动开发采用类似这样的结构：

  • We believe <this change>我们相信 <这个变更>
  • Will result in <this outcome>将带来 <这个结果>
  • We will know we have succeeded when <we see X change in this metric>当 <我们看到这个指标出现 X 变化> 时，我们就知道成功了

For example:

例如：

  • We believe adding a distributed cache我们相信加入一个分布式缓存
  • Will result in faster startup times将带来更快的启动时间
  • We will know we have succeeded if startup time is less than 15 seconds如果启动时间少于 15 秒，我们就知道成功了

Decisions based on data are better than arguing for an hour and defaulting to the loudest voice in the room.

基于数据做决策，胜过争论一小时、最后让嗓门最大的人说了算。

原书第 231 页

A Rose by Any Other Name…
玫瑰叫什么名字都一样……

Titles can be a funny thing in many organizations, with roles and responsibilities varying widely across companies. “Architect” is no different and may in fact be worse. Some companies will award the title of architect to only the select group of people who report to the VP of architecture. Regardless of title, it is quite common for senior developers to be actively involved in decisions that are squarely in the architect’s domain.
在许多公司里，头衔是件挺有意思的事，角色和职责在不同公司间差异巨大。“架构师”也不例外，甚至可能更糟。有些公司只把架构师头衔授予向架构 VP 汇报的那一小群人。但无论头衔如何，资深开发者深度参与那些明明属于架构师领域的决策，是相当常见的事。
Architects are often spread thin and may delegate certain architectural tasks to developers. This not only spreads the workload but also provides an excellent growth opportunity for anyone who aspires to one day be an architect.
架构师常常分身乏术，可能会把某些架构任务委派给开发者。这不仅分摊了工作量，也为那些有志于某天成为架构师的人提供了绝佳的成长机会。
Of course, some companies don’t have the title of architect at all. It bears repeating: regardless of titles, you have people making architectural decisions on your projects. Hopefully, they’re making good ones; you’ll know in a year or two if they did.
当然，有些公司根本就没有架构师这个头衔。值得再说一遍：无论头衔如何，你的项目上总有人在做架构决策。希望他们做的是好决策；一两年后你就会知道他们做得好不好。

Fitness Functions

Many architects and organizations invest heavily in the process of creating the appropriate architecture for a project. However, they don’t often give much thought to how to maintain that architecture over time. Sadly, the second law of thermodynamics applies to software, and without effort to counteract disorder, your architecture will devolve.18

许多架构师和组织在为项目打造合适架构的过程中投入巨大，却往往不太思考如何随时间维护这套架构。可悲的是，热力学第二定律也适用于软件：如果不付出努力去对抗混乱，你的架构就会退化。18

18 In a nutshell, the second law of thermodynamics establishes that, without intervention, entropy within an isolated system will never decrease. In other words, a teenager’s bedroom.
简而言之，热力学第二定律指出：若无外力干预，孤立系统内的熵永远不会减少。换句话说，就是青少年的卧室。

From the first commit, your architecture is changing, and while those steeped in its development may intimately understand the nuance of the key architectural considerations, new team members may not have that background. If you’re not diligent, your customers will be complaining about performance or scalability or some other vital quality attribute.

从第一次提交起，你的架构就在变化。虽然沉浸其中的开发者可能对关键架构考量的细微差别了如指掌，但新加入的团队成员可能没有这个背景。如果你不加勤勉，客户就会开始抱怨性能、可扩展性或其他某个至关重要的质量属性。

The Performance Problem
性能问题

Nate here. Early in my architectural career, I was tasked with fixing a performance problem on an ancient VB6 application. Being new to the project (and the role!), I asked when the performance problem first started, hoping we could tie it to a recent update. When I was told the problem started sometime in the last three years, I knew we had a lot of work in front of us. And I started to question my desire to be an architect.
我是 Nate。在我架构师生涯早期，我被派去修复一个古老的 VB6 应用的性能问题。由于对这个项目（以及这个角色！）都还不熟，我问性能问题最早是什么时候开始的，希望能把它和最近的一次更新联系起来。当我被告知这个问题是过去三年间某个时候开始出现的，我就知道面前有一大堆活了。而且我开始怀疑自己是不是真想当架构师。
原书第 232 页

The Performance Problem (continued)
性能问题（续）

In retrospect, diagnosing the problem didn’t have to be so challenging. Had the team created a fitness function that tested performance on a regular basis, it would have discovered the problem sooner, probably before customers even noticed.
回头看，诊断这个问题本不必这么费劲。如果团队当初建了一个定期测试性能的适应度函数，它本会更早发现问题，很可能在客户察觉之前就发现了。

You could hope that your application somehow avoids devolving into a big ball of mud.19 Or you could be more proactive. You could leverage fitness functions to continuously test your architecture, alerting you when something goes out of band. Essentially, a fitness function measures how closely an architecture comes to meeting the objectives. The concept of fitness functions comes from evolutionary computing. Algorithms are mutated with the results tested—is this mutation a success? Applied to architecture, fitness functions allow you to identify and maintain the key architectural characteristics of your application.

你可以寄希望于你的应用不知怎地避免退化成一个大泥球。19或者你可以更主动一些。你可以利用适应度函数持续测试你的架构，在某个指标越界时提醒你。本质上，适应度函数衡量的是一套架构在多大程度上接近目标。适应度函数这个概念来自进化计算。算法被变异，结果被测试——这次变异成功了吗？把它应用到架构上，适应度函数让你能够识别并维护应用的关键架构特征。

19 Hope is not a strategy. But it is what rebellions are built on.
希望不是一种策略。但它正是叛乱所仰仗的东西。

Fitness functions are tests you create to ensure that a refactoring or new feature doesn’t violate your architecture. You can think of fitness functions as a to-do list for developers from architects as well as lightweight, low-ceremony, governance. Essentially, fitness functions are a set of tests you execute to validate your architecture. For example, you could write tests that ensure the following:

适应度函数就是你创建的测试，用来确保一次重构或一个新特性不会违反你的架构。你可以把适应度函数想象成架构师给开发者的一份待办清单，也是一种轻量、低仪式感的治理。本质上，适应度函数就是你执行的一组测试，用来验证你的架构。例如，你可以写测试来确保：

  • Service calls respond within an average of 100 milliseconds.服务调用平均在 100 毫秒内响应。
  • Cyclomatic complexity shall not exceed 5.圈复杂度不得超过 5。
  • Average response times as the number of users and requests increases are reasonable.随着用户数和请求数增加，平均响应时间保持在合理范围。

Ideally, your fitness functions are all automated and run within your CI/CD pipelines. However, some tests may be manual depending on what you need to test. As an architect, you will identify fitness functions early in a project lifecycle; however, they will evolve and change over time. You should periodically review them to ensure they are still relevant. You may discover a better way to test them as well.

理想情况下，你的适应度函数全都是自动化的，并在 CI/CD 流水线中运行。不过，根据你要测试的内容，有些测试可能需要手动执行。作为架构师，你会在项目生命周期早期识别出适应度函数；然而，它们会随时间演进和变化。你应当定期复查它们，确保仍然有意义。你也可能会发现更好的测试方式。

Architectural Diagrams

Ultimately, like everything else in software engineering, architecture is about communication, and one of the ways you will express yourself is via models. (See Chapter 5 for more about modeling.) There is no shortage of architectural diagrams you could utilize, but you need to know when to use which one and with which audience. An architecture diagram that’s perfect for a developer will be incomprehensible for the VP of engineering.

归根结底，就像软件工程里的其他一切一样，架构关乎沟通，而你表达自己的方式之一就是通过模型。（关于建模详见第 5 章。）你可以使用的架构图毫不稀缺，但你需要知道什么时候用哪张图、对着什么受众用。一张对开发者来说完美的架构图，对工程 VP 来说可能完全不知所云。

原书第 233 页

Before creating any diagram, consider your audience. Is this model for a developer? A fellow architect? A business partner? Sometimes you’ll build a diagram solely for yourself, to help decompose a problem or just explore a possible solution. Diagrams can provide context, explain and manage complexity, and identify quality attributes. From component diagrams to deployment diagrams to sequence diagrams, there is no shortage of options at your disposal. Crafting the right picture at the right moment is an important skill for architects to master. When in doubt, ask yourself whether a given diagram will help you tell the story. If so, by all means build it. If not, don’t be afraid to skip it.

在画任何图之前，先考虑你的受众。这个模型是给开发者看的？给另一位架构师看的？还是给业务伙伴看的？有时你画图纯粹是为了自己，用来帮你分解问题或只是探索一个可能的方案。图可以提供上下文、解释并管理复杂性、识别质量属性。从组件图到部署图再到序列图，你手头毫不缺选择。在恰当的时机画出恰当的图，是架构师需要掌握的重要技能。拿不准时，问问自己：这张图能帮你把故事讲清楚吗？能，那就画；不能，就别害怕跳过它。

Architectural Decision Records

On any software project, you will make a plethora of decisions. Some are small, like naming a variable, while others are more consequential, like choosing a cloud provider.20 Inevitably, you will encounter a fork in the road forcing you to make a tough call regarding how your project should proceed. Architects often have to make decisions with insufficient time and inadequate information. After a few hours or days of deliberation, your team will make a choice and soldier on. But did you take any time to write down why you made the choice you made? The second law of software architecture states: why is more important than how.

在任何软件项目上，你都会做出海量决策。有些很小，比如给变量起名；有些则影响重大，比如选择云服务商。20你不可避免会遇到岔路口，被迫就项目该如何推进做出艰难的抉择。架构师常常不得不在时间不够、信息不足的情况下做决策。经过几小时或几天的商议，团队会做出选择并继续前进。但你有没有花点时间写下你为什么做出这个选择？软件架构第二定律说：为什么比怎么做更重要。

20 Not to shortchange the importance of well-named variables, mind you.
请注意，这并不是要贬低起好变量名的重要性。

Sure, you know what led to that decision, at least in the moment. But what about the person who comes after you? What about you in a few short weeks when today’s crisis dominates your thinking? Architectural decision records (ADRs) turn organizational knowledge into a sequential log that future team members can read to understand how your project arrived at the current day.

当然，你知道是什么导致了那个决策——至少当下知道。但后来者怎么办？几周后当今天的危机占据了你全部思绪时，你自己又怎么办？架构决策记录（ADR）把组织知识变成一份按时间顺序排列的日志，未来的团队成员可以通过阅读它来理解你的项目是如何走到今天这一步的。

ADRs were introduced by Michael Nygard as a way to record the motivation behind decisions. They are not meant to be epic tomes, but they should include enough detail to explain the “why.” While you can create them in nearly any word processing tool, using plain text like Markdown or AsciiDoc is very common.21 Several templates are available on the web, but the basic outline of an ADR includes the following:

ADR 由 Michael Nygard 提出，作为一种记录决策背后动机的方式。它们不该是鸿篇巨制，但应当包含足够的细节来解释“为什么”。虽然你几乎可以用任何文字处理工具来创建它们，但使用 Markdown 或 AsciiDoc 这样的纯文本非常普遍。21网上有若干模板可用，但 ADR 的基本大纲包括以下内容：

21 Using plain text also aids in searchability, which is very important.
使用纯文本还有助于检索，这一点非常重要。

Title

Description of the decision prefixed with a three-digit sequential ID. The ID allows you to easily sort the ADRs in order, allowing you to quickly see the path to today. Use descriptive names.

对决策的描述，前面冠以一个三位顺序编号。这个编号让你能轻松地按顺序排列 ADR，从而快速看清通往今天的路径。使用有描述性的名字。

原书第 234 页

Status

While different organizations may use different statuses, you will typically see the following:

虽然不同组织可能使用不同的状态，但你通常会看到以下几种：

  • Request for comment: This ADR is in active review by the team and relevant stakeholders.征求意见（Request for comment）：该 ADR 正由团队和相关干系人积极评审中。
  • Proposed: This ADR is a work in progress awaiting approval.已提议（Proposed）：该 ADR 尚在进行中，等待批准。
  • Accepted: This ADR has been reviewed and adopted.已接受（Accepted）：该 ADR 已经过评审并被采纳。
  • Superseded: ADRs are immutable, but a later ADR might make an earlier ADR obsolete. The superseded ADR can be updated to point to the overriding ADR.已取代（Superseded）：ADR 是不可变的，但后来的 ADR 可能使早先的 ADR 过时。被取代的 ADR 可以更新为指向覆盖它的那份 ADR。

Context

Every decision involves constraints and unique circumstances. For example, your CIO may have a set of preferred vendors, which may artificially limit your choices. Do not skimp on the context.

每个决策都涉及约束和独特的情境。例如，你的 CIO 可能有一套偏好的供应商，这可能人为地限制了你的选择。在上下文上不要吝啬。

Options

What options did you consider? If you eliminated any from consideration, why?

你考虑了哪些选项？如果排除了其中某些，为什么？

Decision

What did you decide to do? Why did you decide to do it? What options did you reject and why? Again, err on the side of too much information.

你决定做什么？为什么决定这么做？你拒绝了哪些选项，为什么？再说一遍，宁可信息多一点。

Consequences

Every decision you make has consequences (positive and negative). What are the consequences of this ADR? Again, err on the side of too much information.

你做的每个决策都有后果（正面的和负面的）。这份 ADR 的后果是什么？再说一遍，宁可信息多一点。

Governance

How will you ensure that the decision is actually followed? What fitness functions will you create to enforce this ADR?

你如何确保这个决策真正被遵守？你会创建哪些适应度函数来强制执行这份 ADR？

Notes

This section includes other information as needed as well as metadata about the ADR such as author(s), various dates (accepted, superseded, etc.), and approvers.

本节根据需要包含其他信息，以及关于 ADR 的元数据，比如作者、各种日期（接受、被取代等）和审批人。

Real-world examples can be extremely helpful but also hard to come by; after all, most companies aren’t going to publish the inner workings of their software projects on the internet. Thankfully, the results of the first Architectural Katas live training are an invaluable resource for the aspiring architect. Groups of three to five built out the architecture for a health food startup, including ADRs. Their work is available on GitHub. Here are three examples of ADRs: ArchColider, Miyagi’s Little Forests, and Jiakaturi.

真实世界的例子可能极有帮助，但也很难得；毕竟，大多数公司不会把自己软件项目的内部运作发到网上。幸运的是，第一届 Architectural Katas 现场培训的成果，是有抱负的架构师的宝贵资源。三五人一组为一家健康食品初创公司搭建了架构，包括 ADR。他们的成果在 GitHub 上可以找到。这里举三个 ADR 的例子：ArchColider、Miyagi’s Little Forests 和 Jiakaturi。

It is very common for ADRs to include additional diagrams or other supporting material. It may be tempting to omit things that are “common knowledge,” but eventually someone will read your ADRs with completely fresh eyes. What would you need in order to understand the decision if it was your first day on the project?

ADR 中包含额外的图或其他支撑材料是很常见的事。把那些“常识”省略掉可能很诱人，但终有一天会有人用完全新鲜的眼光来读你的 ADR。如果是你到项目的第一天，你需要些什么才能理解那个决策？

原书第 235 页

ADRs are often stored in version control, and some organizations have built simple tooling around their ADRs. Others rely on a wiki, but whatever you choose, make sure it can be searched. Odds are you won’t remember exactly which ADR covered that tricky problem with the network settings. When in doubt, keep things simple: software projects are hard enough already; don’t overcomplicate things needlessly.

ADR 通常存储在版本控制系统中，有些组织还围绕 ADR 构建了简单的工具。另一些组织依赖 wiki，但无论你选什么，都要确保它可以被搜索。你多半不会确切记得是哪份 ADR 涵盖了那个关于网络设置的棘手问题。拿不准时，就保持简单：软件项目已经够难了，没必要把事情无端搞复杂。

Wrapping Up

Architecture is a massive topic taking up several books, videos and podcasts, and countless hours of practice. Many developers aspire to be architects, and for many it is the pinnacle of their career. But being an architect is far more complicated than choosing a frontend library and drawing on the whiteboard.

架构是一个宏大的主题，足以写成好几本书、做成许多视频和播客、耗费无数小时的练习。许多开发者渴望成为架构师，对很多人来说这是职业生涯的顶峰。但当一名架构师，远比选一个前端库、在白板上画几笔要复杂得多。

Architecture requires you to see the bigger picture of the application, identify the key quality attributes, and navigate the trade-offs of decision after decision, all while navigating the politics of your organization communicating up, down, and across the org chart. Being an architect is a challenging but very rewarding path. Hopefully, these guideposts will help you navigate that journey should you choose to make it.

架构要求你看清应用的大局，识别关键质量属性，在一个又一个决策中权衡取舍，同时还要在组织中处理好向上、向下、向跨部门的沟通与政治。当架构师是一条充满挑战但非常有回报的道路。如果你选择走上这条路，希望这些路标能帮你领航。

Putting It into Practice

There’s an old joke about a tourist in New York City asking someone carrying a violin case how to get to Carnegie Hall, to which the musician replies, “Practice.” Architecture is no different: if you want to improve, you need to architect a lot of systems! But few architects get to work on hundreds of systems in a career, prompting Ted Neward to ask: “So how are we supposed to get great architects, if they only get the chance to architect fewer than a half-dozen times in their career?” Ted’s astute observation inspired him to create a set of architectural katas covering a variety of domains, with common constraints and just enough detail to allow ample room for interpretation.

有个老笑话：纽约市一个游客问一个提着小提琴盒的人怎么去卡内基音乐厅，音乐家回答：“练习。”架构也没什么不同：想进步，你就得架构很多系统！但很少有架构师一辈子能架构几百个系统，这让 Ted Neward 发问：“那么，如果架构师一辈子只有不到六次架构的机会，我们又怎么培养出伟大的架构师呢？”Ted 的敏锐观察促使他创建了一套架构道场题，覆盖各种领域，带有共同的约束和恰到好处的细节，留出充足的诠释空间。

You can use architectural katas in many ways.22 You could pick one or let fate decide and spend an hour or two working through it on your own or with a small group. What questions would you need answered to create an architecture? What quality attributes matter most for your kata? What is the most complex or risky part of the application? What scares you most as an architect? What architectural style would you recommend?

你可以用很多方式使用架构道场题。22你可以挑一道，或让命运来决定，然后花一两个小时自己做，或和一个小组一起做。要创建一套架构，你需要回答哪些问题？对你的道场题来说哪些质量属性最重要？应用最复杂或最有风险的部分是什么？作为架构师，你最害怕什么？你会推荐哪种架构风格？

22 Even as a party game. With the right audience, at least.
甚至可以当聚会游戏玩。当然，前提是有合适的听众。

Put your solution aside for a few days or even a few weeks. Take another look. What would you change? Did you miss anything the first time? Would you advise a different approach now? Perform an informal architectural review. What questions do your colleagues have? What are the gaps in your proposed solution? Every month or two, tackle a different kata or continue to refine your previous solution.

把你的方案搁在一边几天甚至几周，再回头看。你会改什么？第一遍有没有漏掉什么？现在你会建议不同的做法吗？做一次非正式的架构评审。你的同事有什么问题？你提出的方案有哪些漏洞？每隔一两个月，做一道新的道场题，或继续打磨你之前的方案。

原书第 236 页

Keen on putting your architectural chops to a sterner test? Get a team together and register for an upcoming live Architectural Katas session on the O’Reilly learning platform. You will get a chance to practice your craft on a real problem in a fun and safe environment.

想把你的架构功底放到更严格的考验下？组个队，去 O’Reilly 学习平台报名参加一场即将到来的 Architectural Katas 现场活动。你将有机会在一个有趣而安全的环境中，拿一个真实问题磨练你的手艺。

Katas also make for an excellent interview technique. Rather than asking questions about the quantity of piano tuners in a given metropolitan area or testing someone’s ability to memorize computer science facts, walk through a kata with them. The questions they ask illustrate how they think and approach problems, and the inevitable collaboration will give you an excellent sense of what it would be like to work with this person on a real project.

道场题也是一种绝佳的面试手段。与其问“某个都市区有多少调琴师”这类问题，或测试某人背诵计算机科学事实的能力，不如和他一起走一遍一道道场题。他提出的问题能展现他如何思考、如何处理问题，而不可避免的协作会让你很好地感受到和这个人在真实项目中合作会是什么样子。
